title: VERTICO. III. The Kennicutt-Schmidt relation in Virgo cluster galaxies
question: Are there significant differences in the Kennicutt-Schmidt law between star forming regions in Virgo cluster galaxies and those of normal, star-forming disks, and does the cluster environment modify the star formation process at sub-kpc scales?

what.value: Orientation parameters (optical inclinations and position angles) and CO(2-1)-to-CO(1-0) line ratio R21 = 0.7

evidence.quote: A summary with the basic properties of the working sample of galaxies can be found in Table [\[tab:sample\]](#tab:sample), orientation parameters are drawn from (cite: Brown2021)

In this paper, we derive the molecular surface densities directly from the VERTICO and HERACLES surveys CO (2-1) integrated intensity maps, assuming a fixed CO (2-1)-to-CO (1-0) line ratio, $R_{21}$, of 0.7 as derived by (cite: Brown2021).

what.value: Global star formation rates, integrated stellar masses, and NUV+WISE4 SFR calibration

evidence.quote: global SFR and stellar masses are adopted from (cite: Leroy2019)

With GALEX NUV and color-corrected WISE3 images for each galaxy, we then apply the NUV+WISE4 SFR calibration from (cite: Leroy2019) to derive spatially resolved SFR maps in units $M_\odot$/yr/kpc$^2$.

what.value: Global HI deficiencies calculated using predicted HI mass from field galaxies at fixed stellar mass

evidence.quote: H I deficiencies are calculated using the predicted H I mass from field galaxies at fixed stellar mass, from (cite: Zabel2022).

what.value: Common distance of 16.5 Mpc to all Virgo galaxies

evidence.quote: Based on (cite: Mei2007), we employ a common distance of 16.5 Mpc to all Virgo galaxies throughout the paper.

what.value: Galactic CO-to-H2 conversion factor alpha_CO = 4.35 M_sun pc^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1

evidence.quote: Throughout the paper we assume a constant Galactic value, $\alpha^{MW}_{\textrm{CO}}=4.35\,M_\odot\,\textrm{pc}^{-2}\textrm{(K km s}^{-1}\textrm{)}^{-1}$ (cite: Bolatto2013), for which the corresponding $X_\mathrm{CO}$ is $2\times10^{20}\,\textrm{cm}^{-2}\textrm{(K km s}^{-1}\textrm{)}^{-1}$.

recipe.goal: Convolve CO(2-1) datacubes and compute Moment-0 integrated intensity maps
recipe.method: Convolve imaged ALMA datacubes to 9" (720 pc) and 15" (1.2 kpc) resolution, apply a spatially and spectrally varying S/N mask (core mask S/N >= 3.5 in >= 3 channels, wing mask S/N >= 2 in >= 2 channels), and integrate along the spectral axis to obtain Moment-0 maps in K km s^-1.
key_parameters: Core mask S/N >= 3.5 in >= 3 consecutive channels; wing mask S/N >= 2 in >= 2 consecutive channels
assumptions: Common distance to all Virgo galaxies = 16.5 Mpc

recipe.goal: Derive molecular gas mass surface density maps
recipe.method: Convert CO(2-1) integrated intensity maps to molecular gas surface density using Sigma_mol = alpha_CO * (I_CO(2-1) / R_21) * cos(i) for both VERTICO and HERACLES samples.
key_parameters: Inclination cut i <= 80 deg for the 37-galaxy subsample
assumptions: Constant Galactic conversion factor alpha_CO = 4.35 M_sun pc^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1 (including 1.36 helium factor)

recipe.goal: Construct spatially resolved Star Formation Rate (SFR) surface density maps
recipe.method: Mask Gaia DR2 stars, subtract background using Astropy Background2D, convolve GALEX NUV and WISE images to 9" using Aniano et al. (2011) kernels, apply a pixel-by-pixel radial linear WISE3-to-WISE4 color correction to WISE3 images, and apply the Leroy et al. (2019) NUV+WISE4 SFR calibration.
assumptions: Kroupa (2003) stellar initial mass function (0.1 to 100 M_sun, slope -2.35 between 1 and 100 M_sun, slope -1.3 between 0.1 and 1 M_sun)

recipe.goal: Fit the resolved Kennicutt-Schmidt relation and compute depletion times and SFE
recipe.method: Fit log(Sigma_SFR) = A + N log(Sigma_mol) using Least Trimmed Squares (LTS) robust linear regression for the ensemble (at 720 pc and 1.2 kpc), HI-deficient vs. HI-normal subsamples (cut at def_HI,M* > 0.3), and individual galaxies; compute SFE_mol = Sigma_SFR / Sigma_mol, tau_dep = Sigma_mol / Sigma_SFR, and Pearson correlation coefficients.

recipe.goal: Analyze azimuthal variations in molecular gas SFE
recipe.method: Sample each galaxy from its optical center with 18 radial vectors in the RA-DEC plane, compute angular separation (0 to 180 deg) to each pixel in the SFE map, and select by eye the reference angle that most cleanly separates the SFE distribution in the resolved KS plot.
key_parameters: 18 radial vectors; angular offsets from 0 deg to 180 deg

score_reason: The high-level analysis recipe, equations, conversion factors, sample tables, and fitting methods are clearly documented and the VERTICO survey products are publicly released via Brown et al. (2021), though full reproduction requires consulting Brown et al. (2021) for CO data products, Roberts et al. (in prep.) for the exact WISE3/WISE4 color-correction fits, and knowing the exact pixel sampling grid and LTS trimming fraction.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA project codes are public, VERTICO high-level moment-0 maps are publicly available, ancillary GALEX/WISE data are archival, and the main results are well-defined numeric KS slopes, intercepts, scatters, and depletion times for both the ensemble and 35 individual galaxies.
